## Summary

- define a strict, versioned local-session trace schema with canonical JSON and JSONL serialization
- add an export CLI for Codex/Claude JSONL, generic JSON, Markdown, and text transcripts
- retain only user/assistant text and minimal provenance while filtering tools, environment data, archives, binary inputs, and common credentials
- document safe export and review practices, distinct from restorable session bundles
- add focused parser, sanitization, archive-rejection, and CLI coverage

## Verification

- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/local-session-trace.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/export-local-session-trace-cli.test.js` — 16 passed
- `env -u GITHUB_OUTPUT npm --prefix .agent run test:runtime` — 772 passed
- `npm --prefix .agent run check:docs` — 5 passed

Closes #492

An opening four-backtick fence is incorrectly closed by an inner three-backtick run because the parser tracks only the character. A subsequent `Assistant:` or `Tool:` line can therefore be reclassified as a transcript boundary. This narrowly affects **Keep docs in sync** and **Prefer simple implementations**.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 0f6f0b8e3960dc057d251fdada15bca7231f4810 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #493 implements the local-session trace foundation split from #489 through #492. It defines a strict versioned schema, sanitizer, export CLI, tests, and documentation for Codex, Claude, JSON/JSONL, Markdown, and text transcripts. Attachment verification, GitHub inspection workflows, and memory/rubrics persistence are intentionally deferred. The overall staged design and scope are sound, but the exported trace must preserve trustworthy message attribution.

## Review

The current head passes CI and all 16 focused tests, but targeted reproductions confirm a trust-boundary blocker and three correctness/resource issues. Reviewer verdicts ranged from `MINOR_ISSUES` to `NEEDS_REWORK`; the synthesis adopts `NEEDS_REWORK` because Claude synthetic and sidechain records are demonstrably exported as ordinary messages.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Claude meta and sidechain records cross the trust boundary | BLOCKING | Claude records marked `isMeta` or `isSidechain` are exported as normal user/assistant messages. This can misattribute synthetic or child-agent content during the planned memory/rubrics inspection stage. |
| Sensitive-block regexes degrade quadratically | WARNING | Repeated unclosed environment/tool tags trigger super-linear backtracking. A current-head reproduction grew from about 75 ms at 5,000 openers to 1.2 seconds at 20,000. |
| Long Markdown fences close too early | WARNING | The parser remembers only the fence character, so three backticks incorrectly close a four-backtick fence and role-like example text becomes transcript structure. |
| The 25 MiB cap is applied after buffering | WARNING | Files and stdin are completely read before their size is checked, so the documented limit does not bound peak memory or unbounded stdin consumption. |
| Clean-checkout setup omits dependency installation | INFO | The first documented build command assumes `.agent/node_modules` already exists, although dependencies and generated output are ignored. |

## Progress

- The current `check` job passes, and independent validation reproduced all 16 focused test passes.
- The implementation remains surgical, adds no release notes, and correctly defers attachment verification, workflow execution, and persistence.
- The existing rubrics review already documents the Markdown-fence issue, so no duplicate inline comment was posted for it.
- Posted four verified inline comments: [Claude filtering](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451478), [sanitizer complexity](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451467), [input buffering](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451463), and [setup prerequisite](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451460). No replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.
- Cosmetic double-redaction output, repeated sanitization, navigation ordering, and intentionally best-effort secret detection were not elevated to required work.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Claude meta and sidechain records cross the trust boundary</summary>

**Cause:** The [Claude extraction branch](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0f6f0b8e3960dc057d251fdada15bca7231f4810/.agent/src/local-session-trace.ts#L328) descends into `message` without first rejecting top-level `isMeta` and `isSidechain` markers. A focused reproduction exported synthetic metadata, sidechain content, and the real request as three ordinary user messages.

**Candidate solutions:** Reject records where either marker is exactly `true` before message extraction, and add separate regression fixtures for both markers.

**Comments:** This is blocking because the parent design will use traces as evidence for user-attributed memory and rubric learning.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Sensitive-block regexes degrade quadratically</summary>

**Cause:** The [lazy block-matching expressions](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0f6f0b8e3960dc057d251fdada15bca7231f4810/.agent/src/local-session-trace.ts#L132) repeatedly scan toward EOF when many opening tags lack a matching closer.

**Candidate solutions:** Replace them with a linear scanner that suppresses recognized tagged blocks, including malformed/unclosed blocks, and add an adversarial scaling regression test.

**Comments:** This is currently a local-CLI warning, but it must be resolved before the parent upload stage processes untrusted traces.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Long Markdown fences close too early</summary>

**Cause:** The [fence state](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0f6f0b8e3960dc057d251fdada15bca7231f4810/.agent/src/local-session-trace.ts#L517) stores only the marker character and toggles on any run of three or more matching characters.

**Candidate solutions:** Store the opening character and run length, require a valid closing run at least as long as the opener, and add four-backtick and nested-fence tests.

</details>

<details>
<summary>The 25 MiB cap is applied after buffering</summary>

**Cause:** [`readInput`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0f6f0b8e3960dc057d251fdada15bca7231f4810/.agent/src/cli/export-local-session-trace.ts#L184) materializes the complete file or stdin stream before comparing `byteLength` with the limit.

**Candidate solutions:** Preflight regular files with `statSync`; read stdin incrementally with a capped accumulator; cover over-limit file and stdin paths.

**Comments:** One reviewer treated this as INFO because the CLI is local-only. The synthesis uses WARNING because the documented limit is currently ineffective and this foundation is intended for a later upload path.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Clean-checkout setup omits dependency installation</summary>

**Cause:** The [quick start](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0f6f0b8e3960dc057d251fdada15bca7231f4810/.agent/docs/usage/local-session-traces.md#L7) begins with the build even though a clean checkout lacks `.agent/node_modules`.

**Candidate solutions:** Add `npm --prefix .agent ci` before the build or link an explicit installation prerequisite.

**Comments:** The rubrics reviewer considered the guide actionable overall; this remains a narrow first-run documentation issue.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The unresolved trust-boundary, parser, and resource-handling findings are concrete branch changes with focused regression tests suitable for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

`NEEDS_REWORK`

## Action Items

- [ ] Filter Claude `isMeta` and `isSidechain` records and add regression tests.
- [ ] Replace the sensitive-block regex path with bounded linear processing and adversarial coverage.
- [ ] Track Markdown fence length and add a four-backtick regression test.
- [ ] Enforce the input limit before or during file/stdin reads and test both paths.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: bf9484e78b37ef66cc0389ccd3dad910865be11a -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #493 delivers the trace-export foundation for [#489](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/489) through the scoped child [#492](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/492). It adds a versioned sanitized schema, export CLI, tests, and documentation for structured and role-labelled transcripts. Attachment verification, inspection workflows, and memory/rubrics persistence are intentionally deferred. The staged design is sound, but the current head still has two message-trust boundary defects.

## Review

Current head `bf9484e7` passes CI, and the earlier fixes for Claude filtering, bounded reads, and sensitive-tag scanning are effective. Current-head reproductions nevertheless confirm two blockers and one sanitizer warning; reviewers differed on the Markdown defect’s severity, but it is blocking here because the parent feature depends on trustworthy user attribution.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Tagged tool wrappers can be exported as user messages | BLOCKING | A typed `tool_result` wrapper containing `messages` is unwrapped before its type is checked, allowing raw tool content to be exported as user-authored text. |
| Markdown fence content can forge user attribution | BLOCKING | A same-length fence with an info string is treated as a closer, so role-like lines inside assistant code can become user messages. |
| PEM redaction is quadratic and leaks unterminated keys | WARNING | The lazy private-key regex scales roughly quadratically across unmatched openers and returns an unterminated key block verbatim. |
| Clean-checkout quick start omits dependency installation | INFO | The first documented build command fails in a clean checkout until `.agent` dependencies are installed. |

## Progress

- The current [check job passes](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/30799194012/job/91639595924); reviewer validation also passed 21 focused tests, 777 runtime tests, and five documentation checks.
- Resolved three verified same-agent threads whose issues are fixed: [bounded reads](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451463), [tag-scanner complexity](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451467), and [Claude meta/sidechain filtering](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451478).
- Posted two new inline comments: [tagged-wrapper leakage](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702668600) and [PEM redaction](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702668612). No replies or minimizations were performed.
- The current [rubrics review](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#issuecomment-5164360199) already covers the fence-parser defect, and the existing [setup-prerequisite comment](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#discussion_r3702451460) remains valid, so neither was duplicated inline.
- The diff remains within the intended foundation scope and does not modify release notes.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Tagged tool wrappers can be exported as user messages</summary>

**Cause:** [`recordsFromJson`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bf9484e78b37ef66cc0389ccd3dad910865be11a/.agent/src/local-session-trace.ts#L536-L539) unwraps every top-level `messages` array before inspecting its wrapper type. A `tool_result` wrapper therefore bypasses the raw-tool exclusion applied by `extractMessage`.

**Candidate solutions:** Reject tool, function, and environment wrapper types before descent, or unwrap only explicitly supported transcript containers. Add regression coverage for typed wrappers containing user-shaped messages.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Markdown fence content can forge user attribution</summary>

**Cause:** The [fence check](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bf9484e78b37ef66cc0389ccd3dad910865be11a/.agent/src/local-session-trace.ts#L652-L659) accepts any matching run prefix as a closer. For example, a three-backtick `js` line inside a three-backtick block closes the parser state even though a closing fence may have only trailing whitespace.

**Candidate solutions:** Recognize openers and closers separately, require a whitespace-only closing suffix and no more than three leading spaces, and add a regression proving role-like code remains attributed to the surrounding assistant message.

**Comments:** Reviewer severities ranged from INFO to BLOCKING. The synthesis uses BLOCKING because the reproduced result creates a false user message that a later rubric-learning stage could treat as an explicit preference.

</details>

<details>
<summary>PEM redaction is quadratic and leaks unterminated keys</summary>

**Cause:** The [private-key expression](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bf9484e78b37ef66cc0389ccd3dad910865be11a/.agent/src/local-session-trace.ts#L272-L275) repeatedly searches toward EOF for unmatched closers. It also leaves a lone `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` block unchanged.

**Candidate solutions:** Scan PEM boundaries in one pass, redact through EOF for an unclosed opener, and add adversarial scaling plus unterminated-key tests.

**Comments:** Both code reviewers identified the quadratic path. It remains a WARNING because this is currently a local CLI with mandatory manual output review.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Clean-checkout quick start omits dependency installation</summary>

**Cause:** The [quick start](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bf9484e78b37ef66cc0389ccd3dad910865be11a/.agent/docs/usage/local-session-traces.md#L5-L12) begins with `npm run build`, while `.agent/node_modules` is ignored and absent from a clean checkout.

**Candidate solutions:** Add `npm --prefix .agent ci` before the build or link an explicit installation prerequisite.

**Comments:** This is optional documentation polish and is already covered by an open inline comment.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The two trust-boundary defects and bounded PEM-redaction change are concrete, focused branch changes suitable for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

`NEEDS_REWORK`

## Action Items

- [ ] Reject unsafe tagged JSON wrappers before unwrapping `messages`, with regression tests.
- [ ] Correct Markdown fence opener/closer recognition and add the user-attribution regression.
- [ ] Replace the PEM regex with linear conservative redaction and cover unmatched input.
